findings.summary: The approvals file is an agent-written approval record that the compiler accepts as an authenticated operator approval; RDP-003 forbids this as written, and the records restate RDP-003 as if it permitted it.
findings.detail: approvals.causa.json (commit 1865da2, author Claude) carries authority {kind: operator, id: kemiller2002}. VerificationPlan.operatorApprovals treats that string as an authenticated operator approval, and the plan and docs call the amendments 'authenticated operator' changes. RDP-003 says 'An agent MUST NOT: write, edit, generate or infer an approval record', and the R5A-001 intake says the R5A-001-11 decisions (DEC-R6-003, -004) are 'recorded by the owner, not transcribed by an agent'. The records say 'RDP-003: an agent's transcription takes effect only when the owner merges the pull request'. That is not RDP-003's text. It is an interpretation that has precedent on main (docs/PROCESS-EVIDENCE-AND-READINESS.md, owner-merged). The file is honestly labelled as a transcription, and nothing in it presents an agent statement as the owner's. This repeats the defect class the Rehearsal 5 audit scored against AR-024-O1 ('None is authenticated as the owner's action'). Remedy: record it explicitly as an RDP-003 deviation that the owner accepts in the PR review, or have the owner commit the approvals file. Either way the owner's authenticated act, not the JSON authority field, should be what makes the amendments authoritative.

findings.summary: UI-015-O2 clause 'legal command enforcement' is mapped to constituents that prove less than the clause.
findings.detail: Its constituents are UI-004-O1 (render only policy-authorized commands) and UI-004-O6 (no parallel policy engine). Neither requires rejecting an illegal or stale command. UI-004-O4 (reject stale-version submissions, safe fault messages, no duplicate submission) and AR-006-O2 (invalid or unauthorized transitions rejected before side effects) state that, and are not constituents. Because the plan says UI-015-O2's own bound tests prove only its residual clauses, enforcement is no longer something UI-015-O2's test is asked to prove, and its constituents do not prove it either. Two weaker cases: 'offline/conflict recovery' relies on UI-010-O1, which designs a recoverable offline state but does not require recovery; 'catalog load and replay' relies on EXT-DATA-013-O2, which needs no browser evidence. DEC-R6-008 authorizes the derivation as recommended, but this mapping was not part of the recommendation's stated consequence. Fix: add UI-004-O4 and AR-006-O2 to 'legal command enforcement' (and a sync or offline-queue obligation to 'offline/conflict recovery'), or make those clauses residual.

findings.summary: The derivation consistency check can be defeated through curation: connectives may be any word of the text, and clause-to-constituent semantics are unchecked. Both weakenings compile (V18 PASS) and are READY.
findings.detail: derivationProblems accepts any connective that is a word of the obligation text, and removes every occurrence of that word from the residue. So a curation can drop whole clauses by declaring their words connectives. Nothing relates a clause to what its constituents state, so every residual clause can be mapped to an unrelated obligation, leaving UI-015-O2 with no residual clause for its own test. The README claim that the clauses and connectives 'account for every word' therefore does not protect the obligation. The committed v3 does not do this. Any such edit produces a new plan digest, so it would surface in review of the pins.

findings.summary: The v3 plan does not validate against the schema shipped in its own package.
findings.detail: requirements-compiled/v3/verification-plan.schema.json is byte-identical to v2's revision-2 schema ($id .../revision-2, root additionalProperties false). The v3 plan, described as 'revision 3', adds scopeDecisions, obligation.amendment and obligation.derivation. jsonschema reports 7 errors on the v3 plan and 0 on v2. docs/VERIFICATION-PLAN-CONTRACT.md tells strict validators to use the schema, so a strict consumer rejects the pinned plan. Fix: ship a revision-3 schema in v3 that declares the three members.

findings.summary: R5A-001-04 is recorded as 'implemented', but review-tag removals take effect only when an optional, unpinned --review-tag-changes file is supplied.
findings.detail: PlanVerification.assess treats ReviewTagChanges = JNull as no removals. No pinned invocation passes the flag: acceptance-process.yml runs only verify-process, and the README's verify-plan example omits it. Omitting the file silently lets a test a review removed count again. That contradicts DEC-R6-008's wording 'A test a review removed from an obligation never counts again'. The listing logic itself works (R6ScopeTests checker passes). Pin the review-tag-changes file, or require it, in the acceptance invocation at kickoff.

findings.summary: A resealed plan with UI-015-O2's derivation removed passes preservation, derivation diagnostics and plan-readiness. Only the digest pins catch it.
findings.detail: derivationDiagnostics only inspects obligations that still carry a derivation. Nothing cross-checks scopeDecisions.derivedObligations (which still lists UI-015-O2) against the obligations. verify-plan has no plan-digest pin, a pre-existing gap documented in PREFLIGHT.md. Without the derivation, UI-015-O2 verifies without its constituents. It is mitigated by plan-readiness --plan-digest and verify-process --plan-digest.

findings.summary: DEC-R6-001 leaves PF-015-O2's read-only-secret versus live-write tension to 'the implementation and the independent reviewer'.
findings.detail: Deciding how PF-015-O2 ('an approved secret ... with least-privilege read-only permissions') is met while the PF-014 live writes need write access is an interpretation of scope. The R6 script reserves such interpretations for the owner ('Do not choose for the owner'). The record correctly does not decide it. However, the suggested second write token would be a new secret, which AR-033 requires to be ready before kickoff, and it needs owner approval. This should be an owner decision before kickoff, not left to the implementer.
